name: Nonprofits
blurb: Grant writing, donor analytics, and service delivery on small budgets, with governance capacity as the constraint, from CEP and NTEN to Candid and the equity project.

points.desc: AI-focused nonprofits and open-source foundations are tracked with sourced classifications.
points.name: Nonprofit AI organisations are catalogued here

points.desc: Census BTOS includes nonprofit-heavy service sectors in its series.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The Center for Effective Philanthropy's sector research, including its AI-focused reporting, examines how foundations and nonprofits use AI for operations, program delivery, and communications.
points.name: CEP examines how the sector deploys AI

points.desc: The Nonprofit Technology Network runs regular sector-wide research on technology investment, digital maturity, and AI policy adoption among nonprofits.
points.name: NTEN surveys nonprofit digital maturity

points.desc: Sector research on AI accessibility, training gaps, and ethical implementation across community organizations.
points.name: The AI Equity Project tracks the access gap

points.desc: The nonprofit data organization behind GuideStar and Foundation Center tracks grantmaking trends, including funding directed toward AI adoption and technology infrastructure.
points.name: Candid tracks the funding side

points.desc: The annual AI Index reports AI's social impact and implementation across mission-driven and public-sector organizations - the citable macro series.
points.name: Stanford HAI measures the macro trends

summary: Grant writing, donor analytics, and service delivery are the practical uses; governance capacity is the constraint. No single entity keeps a real-time registry of nonprofit AI adoption - coverage comes from sector research organizations, and this page names the ones that actually publish it.
